text.en: Near Thiruvakkarai in Villupuram, tree trunks buried 2 million years ago have turned to stone yet still show their rings. They show how fossils give a window into ancient life.

A fossil is any preserved remain or impression of an ancient organism; palaeobotany studies fossil plants and helps in the study of phylogeny and classification.
Kaspar Sternberg is the Father of Palaeobotany and Birbal Sahni is the Father of Indian Palaeobotany.
Fossilization occurs by petrifaction (minerals like silica replace tissue), mould and cast, carbonization, preservation in ice or amber, compression and infiltration.
The age of a fossil is found from radioactive elements; carbon-14 dating was discovered by W. F. Libby (1956) and measures the C-14 remaining after death.
Living fossils such as Ginkgo biloba look like their ancient ancestors.
Thiruvakkarai fossil wood park in Villupuram district preserves tree trunks about 2 million years old that were replaced by silica.
Ethnobotany is the study of plants and their uses through traditional knowledge; the term was coined by J. W. Harshberger in 1895.
Ethnobotany helps nutrition, healthcare, conservation and gives chemists and pharmacologists leads on herbal medicine.
Astrobiology searches for extraterrestrial life; a planet must have the right mass to hold an atmosphere and lie in the habitable or Goldilocks zone where liquid water can exist.
Extremophiles live in extreme conditions on Earth, so similar life might exist in extreme places in our solar system.

problem.en: A fossil bone has 25 percent of its original carbon-14 left. What does this suggest about its age?

text.en: C-14 decays at a steady rate after death.
25 percent left means two half-lives have passed.
So the fossil is roughly 11,000 years old.

prompt.en: Describe two methods of fossilization with an example.

requiredIdeas.en: Petrifaction: silica replaces tissue, as in the Thiruvakkarai fossil wood
Preservation in ice or amber keeps the entire organism
Mould and cast preserves the outer shape

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking fossils are always real bones

points.en: Fossils show gradual evolution; palaeobotany studies plant fossils.
Ethnobotany: traditional uses of plants; coined by Harshberger.
